questions.q: What does Hollis compare breaking promises to yourself to?
a: A friend who keeps cancelling plans with poor excuses
A coach who pushes you too hard
A boss who never explains expectations
A stranger who ignores your messages
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the unreliable friend Sarah to show how we let ourselves down.

questions.q: How does Hollis suggest making self-promises easier to keep?
a: Start with small, realistic steps you can follow through on
Tell everyone about the promise for accountability
Set a strict deadline and a penalty for missing it
Make a fresh promise each morning instead
questions.why: Lesson 1 says keeping goals realistic lets you follow through and retrain your mind.

questions.q: What does Hollis say about chaos in family life?
a: It is a normal part of the job, so embrace it
It signals that you are failing as a parent
It disappears once children start school
It should be minimized with stricter routines
questions.why: Lesson 2 says chaos comes with parenting and you should go with the current, not against it.

questions.q: What does the drowning man story illustrate?
a: You should accept the help that comes your way
You should wait for divine intervention
You should learn to swim before you need help
You should offer help before asking for it
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the man who ignores three rafts to show that nobody can do it all alone.

questions.q: Why did Hollis visualize a specific Louis Vuitton purse?
a: A concrete goal felt achievable and kept her motivated
It was a gift she promised her mother
It reminded her of a childhood ambition
It was cheaper than other rewards she wanted
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a specific object represented her goal, while a vague dream would overwhelm her.
